content.intro: Learn relationship options through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Relationship Options matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines relationship options as part of django models and database fundamentals. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: on_delete; related_name; related_query_name; Nullability of relationships; Related-object lifecycle. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: on_delete
items.text: `on_delete` describes Django’s behavior when the referenced object is deleted. Choose CASCADE, PROTECT, RESTRICT, SET_NULL, or another documented option based on data retention and integrity requirements.

items.title: related_name
items.text: For related_name, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: related_query_name
items.text: related_query_name should be evaluated using a representative workload and a measured baseline. Compare correctness and resource usage before and after the change; the best choice depends on the database backend, request mix and data size.

items.title: Nullability of relationships
items.text: Nullability of relationships affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready.
